The abstract describes an interpretability method (LEF) that, in RAG settings, separates evidence from parametric memory and from retrieved documents. The experiments include detecting RAG source disagreement across models. So the paper does run experiments with RAG systems, namely evaluating the LEF method on them, though RAG is only part of the paper. The rules say to include if the paper runs experiments with a RAG system, and here it does evaluate RAG source disagreement. It is not clearly outside RAG scope, so the choice is between INCLUDE and MAYBE. The RAG experiments appear real ("LEF detects RAG source disagreement on four of six families"), but the paper's main contribution is not a RAG method. Since the rules allow including papers that evaluate RAG, I lean toward INCLUDE.
